monthly_review.summary: This month shows a dramatic collapse in volume and intensity compared to last month, reflecting likely fatigue or external life constraints — not progression.
monthly_review.highlight: The 79.7 km drop from last month — combined with only one run in August so far — is not a blip but part of a steep multi-month decline: total km dropped from 82.4 (Jul) → 61.0 (Jun) → 46.0 (May) → 38.0 (Apr), confirming progressive disengagement or systemic fatigue.

goal_tracker.message: Catching up to last month’s 82.4 km would require ~2.7 km/day for 29 days — impossible given current readiness (training readiness 31/100, 14/14 nights <7h sleep). Chasing this number is medically inadvisable and risks injury or burnout; recovery must precede volume.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated aerobic decoupling
insights.body: Despite improved running economy (13.19 vs 13.64), aerobic decoupling is high (7.09%) — well above the 5% aerobic threshold — and matches the pattern seen in months with <7h sleep (e.g., Jul: 14/14 nights <7h, median decoupling 7.11%). Sleep loss impairs neuromuscular coordination and metabolic efficiency, manifesting as drift even when pace/HR appear controlled.

insights.title: Acute load increased 20.8% while HRV recovery reserve remains shallow
insights.body: Weekly TRIMP rose +93.6 vs baseline (543.6 vs 450.0), yet HRV’s recent average (69.9 ms) is only +9.6 ms above baseline (60.3 ms) — and latest reading (65.0 ms) suggests diminishing returns. This mismatch signals diminishing autonomic resilience despite 'optimal' ACWR.

insights.title: Cadence surged while stride length collapsed — sign of compensatory gait under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence jumped +13 spm (118→131) this month, but stride length dropped to 66.63 cm (vs 70.42–86.42 cm in recent long runs) and ground contact remained stable (~309 ms). This suggests shorter, choppier steps — typical of central fatigue or sleep-deprived neuromuscular control — not improved efficiency.

insights.title: Zone 1 dominance (87%) reflects deconditioning or forced conservation, not base-building
insights.body: This month’s zone distribution (z1: 87%, z2: 12%, z3+: 1%) is extreme — unlike any prior month (e.g., Jul z1 was only 19%). With VO2max stable (39.0) and best efforts unchanged, this isn’t polarized training; it’s avoidance of effort due to low readiness (31/100) and zero recovery time (0.0 hrs).

recommendations.action: Prioritize 7+ hours of sleep for 5 consecutive nights — use body battery trend (currently 71.5 avg) as feedback: if it drops below 65, add 30 min pre-sleep wind-down ritual.
recommendations.reason: 14/14 nights <7h sleep is the strongest driver of compromised readiness, directly impairing HRV, decoupling, and neuromuscular control.
